searchText: Hi, does verkle tree will change to kzg-based in future? <dankrad> no, there is no plan to change it to KZG got it, thank you~ Is this so? There's a bunch of "ethereum.org" subpages that explicitly mention polynomial commitments whenever "verkle" is mentioned. The V is for vector (commitment) afaik. <ralexstokes> both concepts are pointing at the same thing here <ralexstokes> a vector comm is a more general idea than a poly comm <ralexstokes> but we are using IPAs for Verkle tries (which are vector comms but you can just write your poly's coeffs as vector elements and get a poly comm) Ah fine, I interpreted <@555483069038198827>'s reply in a different way <dankrad> The two are very closely related: Every polynomial commitment is (trivially) a vector commitment. Every vector commitment that is also additively linear (i.e. two commitments can be added together and form a new commitment for the elementwise sum) can be turned into a polynomial commitment using IPAs (Inner Product Arguments) We started out by trying to use KZG as our vector commitment, but it turned out simpler Pedersen commitments are a lot faster and more suitable to our usecase Yeah yeah I took your answer as saying that we would implement a minimal verkle tree with Merkle proofs still for a while

<dankrad> The two are very closely related: Every polynomial commitment is (trivially) a vector commitment. Every vector commitment that is also additively linear (i.e. two commitments can be added together and form a new commitment for the elementwise sum) can be turned into a polynomial commitment using IPAs (Inner Product Arguments)

We started out by trying to use KZG as our vector commitment, but it turned out simpler Pedersen commitments are a lot faster and more suitable to our usecase
